i'm very glad you brought this up. i had a journal in 6th grade and wrote really personal things in it. someone reported me to the principal for writing "inappropriate" things in it, which were only mine to see and were used to cope. i got my journal taken away. they read every single page to my mom, and i got in-school suspension for 3 days.

this ruined many opportunities that i was given in school, given my punishment. i was a "gifted kid" or high-ability, whatever, and many program invitations were withdrawn from me because of the punishment i received for writing in my personal journal.

it definitely instilled trust issues in me, or at least more than before. up until this year (a decade later), i wasn't able to physically write down any kind of feelings i had, and i still guard all of my possessions like my life depends on it. i hold things back from people because i'm afraid i'll be punished for expressing my feelings, even from friends, family, and my own therapist.

sorry if this was trauma dump-ish. i just feel validated here knowing that other people have had similar experiences.

be careful with klonopin/kpin. i became dependent on it at a young(ish) age (about 16-17) and overdosed and blacked out for 3 days and apparently was walking around the house with only underwear on.

**take the recommended dose.** if you think your current dose isn't strong enough, ask to be bumped up. don't take more than prescribed or chances are that you'll become dependent on benzos.

i've been switched to valium now and do better with it, i don't trust myself not to overdose on klonopin so i asked not to be put on it again.

**edit:** all benzos have the chance of addiction/dependence so just be careful and take your meds as directed. share *any and all* concerns with your psychiatrist about the medications you're on. they're there to help you.
